title: Saving only the errors
description: Print fruits.txt and missing.txt in one go. missing.txt does not exist, so this produces both normal output and an error. Send only the error into errors.txt, replacing the stale content it holds now. The contents of fruits.txt must still be printed to the terminal, and must not end up in errors.txt.
objective: Practise sending a command's error stream into a file, replacing what was there, while normal output stays on screen.
check:
if ! grep -q 'missing.txt' errors.txt; then
  echo "errors.txt should hold the error about missing.txt. It reads:"
  cat errors.txt
  exit 1
fi
if grep -q 'stale error' errors.txt; then
  echo "errors.txt still holds its old content: it should have been replaced, not added to."
  exit 1
fi
if grep -q 'apple' errors.txt; then
  echo "errors.txt should hold only the error, but the normal output of fruits.txt went in there too."
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qx 'apple' "$CMM_STDOUT"; then
  echo "The contents of fruits.txt should still be printed to the terminal."
  exit 1
fi
if [ -s "$CMM_STDERR" ]; then
  echo "The error still reached the terminal."
  exit 1
fi

title: Adding errors to an existing log
description: Print fruits.txt and missing.txt in one go. missing.txt does not exist, so this produces both normal output and an error. Add only the error to the end of errors.log. The line already in errors.log must survive (the obvious way of sending errors into a file empties it first, and this must not). The contents of fruits.txt must still be printed to the terminal, and must not end up in errors.log.
objective: Practise appending a command's error stream to a file without losing its earlier content.
check:
if [ "$(head -n 1 errors.log)" != 'earlier error' ]; then
  echo "The line already in errors.log was lost: its earlier content was overwritten instead of added to."
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q 'missing.txt' errors.log; then
  echo "errors.log should hold the error about missing.txt. It reads:"
  cat errors.log
  exit 1
fi
if grep -q 'apple' errors.log; then
  echo "errors.log should hold only the error, but the normal output of fruits.txt went in there too."
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qx 'apple' "$CMM_STDOUT"; then
  echo "The contents of fruits.txt should still be printed to the terminal."
  exit 1
fi
if [ -s "$CMM_STDERR" ]; then
  echo "The error still reached the terminal."
  exit 1
fi

title: Hiding error messages
description: Print fruits.txt and missing.txt in one go. missing.txt does not exist, so this produces both normal output and an error. Throw the error away completely: it must not reach the terminal, and it must not be saved in any file in the directory. The contents of fruits.txt must still be printed to the terminal. The command should still report failure, because one of the files really is missing: hiding the message is not the same as fixing the problem.
objective: Practise discarding a command's error stream while keeping its normal output.
check:
if ! grep -qx 'apple' "$CMM_STDOUT"; then
  echo "The contents of fruits.txt should still be printed to the terminal."
  exit 1
fi
if [ -s "$CMM_STDERR" ]; then
  echo "The error still reached the terminal."
  exit 1
fi
extra=$(ls -A | grep -vx 'fruits.txt' || true)
if [ -n "$extra" ]; then
  echo "The error should be thrown away, not saved. These new entries appeared:"
  printf '%s\n' "$extra"
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$CMM_EXIT" = 0 ]; then
  echo "The command reported success, so missing.txt was never asked for. Print both files and hide only the error."
  exit 1
fi

title: Capturing everything in one file
description: Print fruits.txt and missing.txt in one go. missing.txt does not exist, so this produces both normal output and an error. Send both the normal output and the error into all.log, so that nothing at all reaches the terminal. Watch the order you write things in: get it wrong and the error still lands on the screen.
objective: Practise sending a command's normal output and error stream into the same file.
check:
if [ ! -f all.log ]; then
  echo "all.log was not created."
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qx 'apple' all.log; then
  echo "all.log should hold the contents of fruits.txt as well. It reads:"
  cat all.log
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q 'missing.txt' all.log; then
  echo "all.log should hold the error about missing.txt. It reads:"
  cat all.log
  exit 1
fi
if [ -s "$CMM_STDOUT" ] || [ -s "$CMM_STDERR" ]; then
  echo "Nothing should reach the terminal: both the normal output and the error belong in the file."
  exit 1
fi

title: Adding a full run to a build log
description: Print fruits.txt and missing.txt in one go. missing.txt does not exist, so this produces both normal output and an error. Add both the normal output and the error to the end of build.log, so that nothing at all reaches the terminal. The line already in build.log must survive: this run is added after it, not written over it.
objective: Practise appending both a command's normal output and its error stream to the same file.
setup:
printf 'apple
banana
' > fruits.txt
printf '=== earlier run ===
' > build.log
check:
if [ "$(head -n 1 build.log)" != '=== earlier run ===' ]; then
  echo "The line already in build.log was lost: its earlier content was overwritten instead of added to."
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qx 'apple' build.log; then
  echo "build.log should hold the contents of fruits.txt as well. It reads:"
  cat build.log
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q 'missing.txt' build.log; then
  echo "build.log should hold the error about missing.txt. It reads:"
  cat build.log
  exit 1
fi
if [ -s "$CMM_STDOUT" ] || [ -s "$CMM_STDERR" ]; then
  echo "Nothing should reach the terminal: both the normal output and the error belong in the file."
  exit 1
fi
